authorization: User requested VFOPT-UI-026 and continued implementation, then the next work item.
changes: Replace cubic candidate rescans with dense Prim nearest-distance updates; each unordered finite pad pair is evaluated once with linear typed-array workspace.
Preserve Math.hypot comparison, connected insertion-order/pad-index ties, transformed coordinates, ratline IDs, roots, output order and malformed-coordinate compatibility.

Give each PCB synchronization session an owned engine cache; reuse world pad geometry, spanning trees and ratline objects for unchanged nets, and prune removed geometry on updates and empty documents.

Index both directions of trace endpoints using spatial cells while retaining strict 0.05 tolerance and existing coordinate-only routed suppression. Trace changes refresh visibility without rebuilding MSTs.
Keep the existing static API and caller behavior; the synchronization owner supplies its cache. No worker was required for measured 32-512-pad calculations below the 50 ms budget.

conditions: Separate Chrome CDP HeapProfiler sampling lane, three fresh-cache measurements per size/implementation after two warmups; includes allocations collected by minor and major GC.

Profile heads and sample counts retained; sampled byte totals are estimates, not exact allocation counts, retained heap or peak laptop RAM. Only allocations on engine call stacks are attributed; harness/fixture allocation is excluded.
Intervals vary by pad count to keep overhead bounded, with the same interval for each before/after pair. Profiler timings are deliberately excluded from latency measurements.
Before uses the preserved pre-change engine; current and legacy execute on the same fixture in the same browser process. No external HTTP or backend work.

measurements.interpretation: Matching fixture/output hashes. Algorithm timing, allocation sampling and browser drawing are separate lanes. Allocation totals are sampled cumulative estimates, not peak/retained RAM. Movement p95 passes; one paired release observation does not establish release p95, and final-redraw acceptance remains pending. Host power/concurrent load are not controlled.

acceptance.criterion: Compare 32/64/128/512-pad nets and report time and allocation growth.
acceptance.detail: 32/64/128/512-pad fixtures have five GC-separated and twenty warm fresh-cache Node timing samples; browser has five movements per size; three allocation profiles per size/version capture sampled cumulative engine allocation, including collected objects. Exact distance-call counts and heap-delta limitations are recorded.

acceptance.criterion: Ratlines preserve equivalent net connectivity, deterministic tie behavior and routed-net suppression.
acceptance.detail: Exact output/fixture hashes match all measured sizes. Oracle comparisons cover insertion-order ties, 100 deterministic randomized graphs, rotations, overlap, negative/large coordinates, missing endpoints, merges/splits, trace tolerance and reversed routing. Cached edits and lifecycle/undo/reload regression checks pass.

acceptance.criterion: Pointer work remains within the interaction budget during PCB drag.
acceptance.detail: 60-second actual 512-pad drag: event-to-footprint-draw p95 27.1 ms; no calculations/publications during movement and one placement commit. Connected-movement calculations peak at 5.3 ms. Final ratline-layer redraw still takes 464.3 ms in the paired release; full release-to-redraw acceptance remains open under VFOPT-UI-027.

fullTest.scope: TypeScript, lint and all existing worker, result, runtime, model, presentation/proposal, board, MNA, scope, canvas, AVR, document, palette, routing, drag and PCB-sync suites plus 15 new ratline contracts.
warnings: Existing Vite dependency-scan shutdown warnings in two SSR presentation harnesses; all assertions and the full command pass. No AI implementation changed.

scope.preserved: Only RatlineEngine, its schematic synchronization cache ownership and package scripts changed among inventoried source files. All backend/configuration, canvas/simulator, PCB store/scene, lockfile, staged pinRegistry.ts and old report bytes match task start. No staging, commits, backend writes or AI implementation changes.

remainingValidation.detail: The paired mouse release final ratline-layer draw improved from 1875.4 ms to 464.3 ms but still exceeds 50 ms. Calculation itself fell from 1212.1 ms to 5.2 ms. Remaining work outside the calculation entrypoint must be profiled in the PCB scene; this is not a fully closed release-latency result.

Regrouping current pad references is linear. Trace changes revisit cached edges, and dense coincident endpoint buckets can still scan many candidates. Math.hypot and per-net output/point objects still allocate; 17 bytes per pad describes typed workspace payload only. Malformed nonfinite geometry uses the slower compatibility path.

Larger than 512-pad nets, large coincident trace sets, sustained whole-laptop CPU/heap, physical pointer-to-display latency, live account persistence/STOMP, manufacturing services and production CSP were not validated by these fixtures. The tested range is not a declared supported product maximum.
Prior schematic rendering, representation and live-validation limitations remain open; their implementation records and historical evidence are preserved.
